text: A pipe open at both ends has a fundamental frequency f in air. The pipe is now dipped vertically in a water drum to half of its length. The fundamental of the air column is now equal to
explanation: For a pipe of length L open at both ends, the fundamental frequency (f) in air is given by the equation: f = v/λ = (v / 2L) ⇒ λ =2L Now, when the pipe is dipped vertically in water and half of it is submerged, the length of the air column is halved. ⇒ L' = L/2 ⇒ λ' =4L' = 2L Hence, f' = v / λ' = v / 2L = f

text: The displacement of a traveling wave is given by y = C sin(2π / λ)(at - x) where t is time, x is distance, and λ is the wavelength, all in SI units. The frequency of the wave is
explanation: The given displacement of a traveling wave is: y = C sin( (2π / λ) (at - x) ) Here: C is the amplitude,t is time,x is distance,λ is the wavelength,a is a constant related to the velocity of the wave. The general form of a traveling wave is: y(x,t) = A sin(kx - ωt + φ) Where: k = 2π / λ is the wave number,ω = 2πf is the angular frequency,f is the frequency. From the equation, we can see that the wave is traveling with a velocity v = a. This velocity is related to the wavelength and frequency by: v = λf So, we can equate: a = λf Solving for f, the frequency: f = a / λ Correct Answer: (d) a / λ

text: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is [NEET 2023]
The 4th overtone of a closed organ pipe is the same as that of the 3rd overtone of an open pipe. The ratio of the length of the closed pipe to the length of the open pipe is: [NEET 2023]
explanation: Harmonics in a closed organ pipe: For a closed organ pipe, the fundamental frequency is produced with a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. The harmonics are only odd-numbered (1st, 3rd, 5th, etc.). The 1st harmonic (fundamental) has the wavelength: λ₁ = 4L (where L is the length of the pipe).The 2nd harmonic is the 3rd overtone (and so on). Harmonics in an open organ pipe: For an open organ pipe, the fundamental frequency has antinodes at both ends. The harmonics are all integer multiples of the fundamental (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.). The 1st harmonic (fundamental) has the wavelength: λ₁ = 2L.The 2nd harmonic is the 1st overtone, the 3rd harmonic is the 2nd overtone, and so on. Given: The 4th overtone of the closed pipe corresponds to the 3rd overtone of the open pipe.In a closed pipe, the 4th overtone corresponds to the 9th harmonic (because only odd harmonics are present).In an open pipe, the 3rd overtone corresponds to the 4th harmonic. Now, let's use the fact that the frequency for both pipes should be the same for the given harmonics. For a closed pipe (where only odd harmonics are present): The 9th harmonic has a wavelength λ₉ = 4L/9. For an open pipe: The 4th harmonic has a wavelength λ₄ = 2L₁/4 = L₁/2. Since the frequency is the same for both pipes, we set the wavelengths equal to each other: λ₉ = λ₄ So, we have: 4L/9 = L₁/2 Solving for the ratio of the lengths: L/L₁ = 9/8 Correct Answer: (c) 9 : 8
